title: RNAseq analysis of blood specimens from ART-suppressed people with HIV prior to analytical treatment interruption
description: Blood from ART-suppressed people with HIV (PWH) were characterized by bulk RNAseq analysis of total PBMCs, or of purified CD4+ T cells from PBMCs. Specimens were obtained from four cohorts: CLEAR, TEACH, REDUC, and ACTG A5345. All participants enrolled in these cohorts underwent analytical treatment interruption (ATI) and were monitored for time-to-rebound of HIV viremia. Overall design: Included are seequencing files generated from clinical trial specimens of people with HIV (PWH) who underwent analytical treatment interruption (ATI). All specimens were obtained before analytical treatment interruption, and the primary association of the study was the time it took for viral rebound during the ATI. Specimens from four trials are included. Three trials were interventional trials performed in Denmark: CLEAR wherein participants orally received the latency reversal agent (LRA) panobinostat for 8 weeks (n=9 participants), REDUC wherein participants received therapeutic vaccination followed by intravenous administration of romidepsin as an LRA (n=16 participants), and TEACH wherein participants received the TLR9 agonist lefitolimod as both an LRA and an immune-boosting agent (n=9 participants). The fourth trial was the AIDS Clinical Trials Group (ACTG) trial A5345, a prospective study wherein individuals underwent ATI in the absence of any therapeutic intervention (n=41 participants). Bulk RNAseq was performed on either total PBMCs (CLEAR, REDUC, TEACH), or purified CD4+ T cells (A5345).
